action_args.justification: The series is seasonally dominated (strength 0.76) with no clear trend, and the model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.123) with high error correlation (mean 0.891, only 3 independent groups). Under these conditions, a robust DTW barycenter (DBA) that respects the seasonal shape of each model's forecast without chasing per-window noise is the natural winner. The runner-up (plain mean, 0.678) is not statistically distinguishable from the leader (0.653), and my own trimmed_mean (0.689) confirms that no simple re-weighting of the full pool improves on the barycenter. With only 3 validation windows, fitted weights carry high variance and are unlikely to beat a shape-preserving robust combination.

6. **Key observation**: The full pool (19 models) strategies outperform all subset strategies. This makes sense because with high correlation (0.891) and unstable rankings, averaging over more models provides more robustness.
